overview: Black meets 2.d4 with ...d6, a Pirc or Philidor-like set-up with the knight already on c6. After 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 White has a free centre and a small space edge; Black waits and aims for ...e5 or ...g6/...Bg7 and ...Bg4. Black is a little cramped, but sound.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Nc3, Nf3, Be2 or Bd3 and castle, keeping a space edge.
Push d5 to drive the knight back, or play Be3 and Qd2.

black_ideas.idea: Play ...Nf6, ...g6 and ...Bg7 or ...e5 to challenge d4.
Pin or exchange to relieve the cramp.

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on d4/e4 against ...d6 and a ...g6/...e5 set-up.

character.notes: Black's position is cramped but hard to break down; White has no easy forcing continuation.

soundness.notes: Playable if slightly passive for Black.

structure.notes: Centre tension with ...e5 or ...d5 yet to come.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom use the Nimzowitsch at all.

character.reason: Neither especially forcing nor especially solid.

structure.reason: Centre not yet decided with ...e5/...d5 still pending.

approach.reason: The Nimzowitsch is seldom chosen by strong players.

plans.reason: White's central space is the theme.
